tree.name: 3D Vehicular Combat
tree.description: Battlezone/Globatis-inspired: 3D vehicle combat, holes on miss, shattering-fragments destruction, sound. GPT-6 Astra, Linux only.

nodes.objective: Build a real-time 3D game (real 3D rendering engine — vector or low-poly) whose centerpiece is physically convincing destruction: when a target is destroyed it shatters into many small blocks that fly upward with random spins and random velocities, then crash back down under gravity and bounce and roll across the ground, with strong sound effects — a deeply satisfying, visceral payoff. The game around this mechanic is yours to design and is NOT fixed to any genre: it could be combat, survival, puzzle, or anything else — but it must be a real game with genuine tension and interactivity (threats that come at you or shoot at you, a challenge to survive or win, a reason to act), not merely free-roam target practice. Make the destruction feel physically real and the loop viscerally fun. Deliver a Linux-runnable artifact (Linux only).
nodes.completion_contract:
Outcome: a runnable Linux real-time 3D game whose centerpiece is physically convincing destruction — targets shatter into small blocks that fly up with random spins and velocities, fall under gravity, and bounce/roll, with strong sound — wrapped in a genuine game (real threat, challenge, a reason to act). Verified by actually running it.
Evidence: source + automated tests + captured runtime evidence (screenshots/frame dumps/recordings) showing the 3D rendering and the destruction physics.
Validation: G plays it and confirms the destruction is viscerally satisfying (blocks fly, spin, fall, bounce, with sound) and the game around it has real tension and is genuinely fun. Sound and destruction physics are first-class, not afterthoughts.

nodes.objective: Establish G12's bounded game design and prove its Linux runtime and validation path before feature implementation.
nodes.completion_contract: Outcome: inspect the configured ai-game-05 repository and available Linux environment; choose a real 3D engine with rigid-body physics and audio; specify one compact game loop with player agency, threatening opposition, explicit win/loss conditions, and destruction essential to success. Genre is unrestricted. Define module interfaces and a concern-by-concern implementation order, keeping scope within the authorized budget. Evidence: saved design and acceptance checklist, reproducible setup commands, and an actually executed minimal engine scene demonstrating 3D rendering, a falling colliding rotating body, and audio output or a captured audio signal. Validation: rerun the scene and inspect its evidence; distinguish signal generation from audible playback and document how G will perform interactive visual and audible validation. Identify real environmental blockers rather than substituting fabricated evidence.

repository_initial_state: Cloned configured URL; empty repository, unborn main
